data.description:
## Description
**What**: Wire /dso:implementation-plan to emit an INTENT_ALLOCATION_IMPLPLAN: JSON ticket comment on the parent story (temp-file write). For each task AC mint a stable intent_id; when reassigning a story DoD to a task preserve the intent_id and set deferred=false; populate test_artifact with the task's proposed test path (kind=new) or an existing test path (kind=existing).
**Why**: Completes the three-stage emit chain so the manifest carries ownership all the way to task-level test artifacts, which downstream consumers (411b, 7f42) read.
**Scope**:
- IN: impl-plan emitter on the parent story; intent_id preservation on DoD-to-task reassignment; test_artifact path+kind population.
- OUT: brainstorm/preplanning emitters (sc-2/3); read/validate (sc-5/6).

## Done Definitions

- A /dso:implementation-plan run posts one INTENT_ALLOCATION_IMPLPLAN: comment on the parent story with one entry per task AC carrying a slug-regex intent_id ← Satisfies: sc-4
- When a task reassigns a story DoD, the emitted entry reuses that DoD's intent_id and sets deferred=false ← Satisfies: sc-4
- Each entry populates test_artifact with kind=new and a proposed test path, or kind=existing and a path that exists on disk ← Satisfies: sc-4
- When this story is complete, the INTENT_ALLOCATION_IMPLPLAN comment is written through ticket-comment-from-file.sh via a temp file rather than an inline argument, so large stories do not hit ARG_MAX ← Satisfies: sc-4
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic in the implementation-plan emitter ← Satisfies: sc-4

## Considerations

- [Stability] DoD-to-task reassignment preserves the story-stage intent_id; a fresh mint would break the stage-precedence merge in read.sh.
- [ARG_MAX] Route the comment body through a temp file via ticket-comment-from-file.sh; inline JSON in a comment argument breaks on large stories.
- [Attribution] kind=existing references a test path that the planner asserts verifies the intent; static checks cannot confirm semantic coverage (known unmitigated edge per epic blue-team).

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As an engineer running /dso:implementation-plan, I want an INTENT_ALLOCATION_IMPLPLAN comment mapping task ACs to test artifacts, so that intent ownership reaches the task layer.
